items.topic: Batch a week of reels in one afternoon
items.caption:
Film a week of reels in one afternoon 🎬 Save this for your next batch day.

The system:
1. Pick 7 ideas before you touch the camera
2. Write only the hooks, bullet the rest
3. Film in batches: talking shots, b-roll, voiceovers
4. Edit inside one template
5. Schedule the whole week in one sitting

slides.title: Pick 7 ideas first
slides.body: Never start a filming day without the list. Ideas on Sunday, camera on Monday.

slides.title: Write hooks only
slides.body: Don't script every word. Write the first line of each reel, then bullet the rest.

slides.title: Film in this order
items: All talking shots in one outfit

slides.title: Edit in one template
slides.body: Same font, same caption style, same intro length. Every decision you skip is speed you keep.

slides.title: Schedule the week
items: Schedule them and stop thinking about it

slides.text: Consistency is a system, not a mood.

items.topic: 3 hook formulas: callout, proof first, versus
items.caption:
Your reel isn't bad. Your first line is. 👇

3 hooks that stop the scroll:
1. The callout: name exactly who it's for
2. Proof first: show the result before the how
3. Versus: two options, one clear winner

Then write 10, score each out of 10, and post the winner.

beats.vo: Your reel isn't bad. Your first line is.
Use one of three hooks. Callout, proof, or versus.
Callout. Name exactly who it's for. If you edit reels at 2 a.m., stop scrolling.
Proof. Show the result before the how. This edit took four minutes. Here's how.
Versus. Two options, one winner. Phone or camera for reels?
Write ten hooks. Score each one. Post only the winner.
